D006-D010_h001.question:
I’ve been off for about a year now—things started getting bad 10 months ago. At work, I was pushing hard, way harder than before. I’d start three or four projects at once, bouncing from machine checks to reorganizing the schedule to rewriting safety protocols no one asked for. My crew said I was snapping over small stuff—a misaligned label, a tool out of place—and I couldn’t sit still, like my skin was crawling. That part’s still here sometimes—like bugs under my clothes, but the doctors find nothing.  

About eight months in, I started hearing myself make up words—like “glarving” when I meant a faulty circuit, or “threm” for someone watching me. I know how it sounds. I *know* there’s no wire tap, but someone’s tracking me—I feel eyes, and the crawling on my skin never really leaves.  

The last few months were different—I just stayed in the garage, didn’t want to see my wife, my guys. Sometimes I’d think, “Wouldn’t it be easier if I just didn’t wake up?” But no plan, just… quiet.  

The highs, the thoughts, the sensations—they overlap. I can’t say which comes first anymore.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h001.answer: C & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—about a year, maybe a bit more. Some days, I feel like I’m on top of the world. I don’t need sleep, my mind races, and everything feels alive—the shadows on the wall, the patterns in the wallpaper, even the clock ticking pulls my attention like it’s shouting at me. I’ll start talking and the words just spill out, sometimes jumping around so much even I can’t follow them. My daughter says she can’t understand me anymore.

There are times I see people standing in the corners of rooms—my late wife, once, or strangers watching me. I know, rationally, they’re not real, but they look so solid. I’ve started thinking the neighbors are spying through the vents, planting things in my mail. I don’t trust the TV either—the newscasters blink too much, like they’re sending me coded messages.

Before all this, I just stopped caring. I didn’t want to fish, didn’t want to see anyone. I even laid out my pills once, thought about ending it. But that passed—now I’m back to feeling electric, like I could fix the whole house in one night. Truth is, I can’t tell when one state ends and the other begins. The voices and visions don’t always go away when the high does. Or maybe they do—I’m not sure anymore.
D006-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
D006-D010_h002.answer: C & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) & Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h003.question:

My mind races, I’m up for hours at night rearranging inventory for no reason, and then I’ll crash. One minute I feel invincible, like I could take over a pharmaceutical conference and rewrite the dosing guidelines on the spot, and the next I’m snapping at customers over nothing.  

The voices started around eight months ago—mostly a man’s voice saying things like, “She knows you’re special,” even when I’m alone. I keep thinking my manager, Dr. Lin, is sending me secret signals—he doesn’t say it, but I *know* he feels something. We’ve never talked about it, but the way he hands me files... it’s meaningful.  

Then came this numb spell last winter. Got a promotion and didn’t care. Felt this sudden urge to step off the subway platform when the train came—no plan, just a pull. It passed, but it scared me. The voices don’t stop, even when I’m not revved up. But I can’t say exactly how long they last without the racing thoughts—maybe a few days at most? I can’t tell when one symptom stops and another starts anymore.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D006-D010_h004.question:

I’d list three properties by noon, start redesigning my office, then impulsively book open houses across town. I had so many ideas, but nothing ever got finished. That went on for months—maybe close to a year. I felt unstoppable, like the world was handing me signs, *winks*—like license plates or strangers’ comments were meant just for me. When that high faded, it dropped hard. I stopped answering calls—even from clients. My daughter worries, but I can’t pretend to be okay. I’ve thought about how it might be easier if I weren’t here. There’s a bridge near my old home, quiet at night… I’ve imagined driving there, what I’d do.

D006-D010_h005.question:

The voices don’t stop, even when I’m not high or down. I can’t tell what’s real anymore. I don’t know if they come with the mood swings or if they’re their own thing.

D006-D010_h006.question:

I’m always moving, fixing things, starting projects—rewired the whole house, redid the gutters, bought a generator… never finish one thing, but I don’t care. Small stuff sets me off, though. My wife asked me to hang a picture last week, and I yelled at her like she’d betrayed me. I know it’s too much, but the anger just erupts.

There’s this smell—like burning plastic or dead wires—it follows me everywhere. I used to think it was the panels overheating on the roof, but I’ve checked them. Nothing’s burning. It’s in my truck, in the house, even outside. And I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced something big’s coming. The grid’s going to fail. The sun’s going to wipe everything clean. Not in years—*soon*. Like, any day now. The world’s rotting from the inside.

She says I’m not making sense. I told her the air itself is toxic, that the government’s hiding the data. I keep working because if I stop, I think I’ll vanish. But I don’t know… do I only think this when I’m wired like this? Or does it stay, even when I’m not? I can’t tell the difference anymore.

    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D010_h007.question:

I also know now that I’m part of a select group—chosen, really. I receive encrypted messages through the radio frequencies at work. It’s why I’m so alert. I don’t know if it’s happening all the time or just with the highs—I can’t tell where one starts and the other ends. It’s all blurred together.

D006-D010_h008.question:

I get snapped at on team chats because I’m irritable, hypersensitive to tone. But how do I explain that I’m the only one preparing for what’s coming? That I see what others don’t?  

The highs and the visions—they come together, as far as I remember. I can’t say for sure if one ever lasted without the other. It’s all blurred.

    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D010_h009.question:

The visions come and go. So does the mood—the drive, the energy. But even when I’m not racing through projects, I still feel certain: it’s all collapsing. I can’t shake it. The thoughts don’t just happen during the highs—they linger. Or at least, I can’t tell if they do. It’s all blurred together.

D006-D010_h010.question:

D006-D010_h011.question:

But then… nothing. A few months back, I just flatlined. No anger, no joy—just this heavy numbness. I kept going over old things—times I snapped at my mom, missed a call. I kept thinking I’d ruined everything and didn’t even care *enough* to fix it.  

The voices? Wait—no, I didn’t say voices. The figures I see… they don’t speak. And I don’t know if what I’m feeling now is a crash or just… who I am.

D006-D010_h012.question:

D006-D010_h016.question:
